current.text: Brooklyn does not own its first-round pick this season. The pick goes to Houston, so the Nets have no draft reason to tank.
The Nets also have no team-building reason to win beyond player development. Their March minutes are uncertain, and veterans like Julius Randle may be rested while the team experiments.
The team plans to try to win while also running a development and evaluation season.
Brooklyn is expected to be one of the worst teams in the league. Slater predicts about 28 wins, with a range of roughly 22 to 30. The win total of 24.5 ranks 29 of 30.
Only rookies and second-year players are available at point guard, which could limit the team's ceiling.
The projected starters are Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe.
Day'Ron Sharpe is expected to start at center. Check early in the season that this actually happens.
The projected bench rotation is Keon Ellis, Noah Clowney, Mo Wagner, Danny Wolf and Nolan Traore. Three of them are big men. Our depth chart lists Terance Mann in the second unit instead of Clowney.
Many young players have a case for minutes, mostly in the second unit and in the frontcourt. Minutes will be hard to find for all of them.
The center spot is open. Center minutes will probably be a messy three-way split between Sharpe, Wagner and Wolf, with some small-ball minutes for Randle and Josh Minott.
Julius Randle will handle the ball a lot.
The second half of the season is uncertain. Brooklyn could shift minutes to young players such as Josh Minott, Noah Clowney, Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Demin.
Michael Porter Jr. is a trade candidate.
The Nets will likely keep making moves. They could also be used as a dumping ground for other teams' players.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, among the most in the league, so rest risk for its veterans is higher.
The fantasy playoff schedule is average: 3, 4 and 3 games in weeks 19 to 21, with only one back-to-back, in week 20.

durable.text: Coach Jordi Fernandez wants several ball handlers and connective playmakers rather than one traditional point guard.

note: Brooklyn will be bad, but Houston owns its pick, so there is no tank reason. Development goals still make March minutes uncertain for veterans like Randle and Porter, and Porter could be traded. Randle and the young guards Brown and Demin should get plenty of the ball, while the center job is a messy split, so watch early whether Sharpe really starts and pulls away from Wagner and Wolf.
